newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money unchanged in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money unchanged in quiet trade.

text.p: * Banks opt to stay liquid over long weekend
The Philippine interbank call loan rate remained at 11.0625 percent in a lacklustre session as banks opted to stay liquid ahead of the long weekend, traders said.
Turnover was thin with only 11.412 billion pesos changing hands between 11.03125 percent and 11.1875 percent.
"The system is very liquid, despite today being the last day of the month," one trader said.

Some financial institutions limited their activities since many of their workers have been given the afternoon off ahead of a national holiday on Friday. Financial markets will closed tomorrow as Filipinos honour their dead on All Saints' Day.
Government offices have been ordered closed starting noon, but Central Bank said cheque clearing will continue until the close of normal business hours.
"Everybody wants to get out of the office as early as possible. There was very minimal trade in the market," one trader added.
The secondary Treasury bills market was also quiet since banks wanted to keep cash on hand in anticipation of massive withdrawals over the weekend.
Secondary rates have remained stable with three month bills bid from 11.55 to 11.625 percent and offered at 11.40 to 11.525 percent.
Six-month bills were bid at 11.95 to 12.25 percent and offered at 11.785 to 11.95 percent, while one-year bills were bid at 11.625 to 11.75 percent and offered at 12.5 to 12.60 percent.
